---
title: "Formal realization schema"
subtitle: "The Phase 8 OWL/SHACL reference encoding of the constructive-realization vocabulary."
---

This page is the course-facing reference for the academy's **formal**
constructive-realization schema (Phase 8). Where
[Constructive realization](constructive-realization.qmd) names the five terms
in natural language and maps them onto the Pico pipeline, this page points at
the machine-readable **Turtle** encoding of the same vocabulary and quality
gate.

Phase 8 is reference-only and opt-in. Nothing here changes how a Pico is
built, and no artifact validates against these files unless it opts in. If you
are writing a lesson or lab, keep authoring Constraints in natural language
as [the Phase 1 vocabulary](constructive-realization.qmd#the-five-terms)
requires; treat the files on this page as a formal restatement you can link
to, not an authoring format.

The reference files live in
[`templates/constructive-realization/`](../../templates/constructive-realization/):

- [ontology.ttl](../../templates/constructive-realization/ontology.ttl) —
  the classes and relations.
- [quality-gate.schema.ttl](../../templates/constructive-realization/quality-gate.schema.ttl)
  — the operational quality gate.
- [hello-pico-instances.ttl](../../templates/constructive-realization/hello-pico-instances.ttl)
  — the concrete `Hello, Pico!` record.

## What the formal schema adds

The informal terms and the formal names describe the same thing. The formal
schema gives each concept a stable identifier you can reference and, on a
small size, a way to state the quality gate precisely.

| Informal (Phase 1)        | Formal (Phase 8)            |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Definition                | `oee:Definition`            |
| Realization               | `oee:Realization`           |
| Element                   | `oee:Element`               |
| Constraint                | `oee:Constraint`            |
| Validation                | `oee:Validation`            |
| (a Definition's conditions) | `oee:hasConstraint`       |
| (an Element's link to its Definition) | `oee:conformsTo` |
| (a Validation's check of an Element)  | `oee:checks`       |

## The Hello Pico record

The reference instance data expresses, in formal form, the same path the
course already teaches:

```text
Definition -> Realization -> Element -> Validation
```

- **Definition** — `hello-pico-definition` names three Constraints:
  exact output, Kubernetes Job form, and successful completion.
- **Realization** — `hello-pico-realization-v1` realizes the Definition and
  uses the Sandcastle, Crossplane, and MiniKube Dependencies.
- **Element** — `hello-pico-job-001` conforms to the Definition and carries
  the observed output `Hello, Pico!`.
- **Validations** — three checks, one per Constraint, each recorded as `passed`.

## Relationship to the phases

- Phases 1–7 keep formal OWL/SHACL out of scope and express shape rules with
  `metadata.yaml` fields and natural-language Constraints.
- Phase 8 re-states those same shape rules as reference triples. The formal
  schema mirrors the Phase 4 `hello-pico-v1` checkable profile and the
  Phase 1–6 vocabulary; it never replaces them.

See [Constructive realization](constructive-realization.qmd) for the Phase 1
vocabulary, [Hello Pico as a constructive exemplar](hello-pico-exemplar.qmd)
for the first concrete exemplar, the [Glossary](glossary.qmd) for one-line
definitions, and `templates/README.qmd` (in-repo scaffold, not published as a
learner page) for the Phase 8 contract.
